summary: Represent a default import as a live indirect binding to the target default export.

target.notes: Default imports use normal indirect-binding semantics; whether the target changes depends on how default was exported.

caveats: export {x as default} is live with x, while export default x initializes a separate default binding from the expression value.

tests.name: default alias can be live
tests.input:
// a.mjs: export let x=1; export {x as default}; export const set=v=>x=v
// b.mjs: import x,{set} from './a.mjs'; set(2); console.log(x);

tests.name: default expression is captured
tests.input:
// a.mjs: let x=1; export default x; x=2
// b.mjs: import x from './a.mjs'; console.log(x);
